name: Short Calendar Straddle (Reverse Straddle Swap)
summary: Buy the front-month straddle and sell the back-month straddle at the same strike; a net-credit, long-near-gamma, short-back-vega structure that goes fully naked after the front legs expire.
max_profit: Approximately the net credit received, when the underlying moves far from the strike by front expiry.
max_loss: UNDEFINED. Worst case before front expiry is a pin at the strike. After front expiry both short back legs are naked - unlimited upside loss on the call and (strike x 100) downside loss on the put per contract.
breakevens: Profitable outside a band around the strike, roughly strike +/- (1.0 to 1.2) x credit in underlying points at front expiry.

greeks.gamma: positive into front expiry (2x a single reverse calendar)
greeks.vega: negative, 2x - the point of the trade

when_to_use: Only in steep contango (back_IV - front_IV >= 6 vol points) with IV rank > 65 and a thesis that back-month vol is mispriced high. Almost always dominated by a simple short strangle or a ratio structure. Kept in the bank for completeness and for the rare post-shock term-structure inversion trade.
entry_rules: REQUIRES ALPACA OPTIONS LEVEL 4. Two naked shorts after front expiry. The automation must reject this at level 3.
back_IV - front_IV >= 6.0 vol points AND IV rank > 65.
ATM strike, |delta| 0.45-0.55, single strike for all four legs.
Credit >= 25% of the back-month straddle premium.
Size on naked-straddle margin, not credit; assume ~$5,000-$15,000 per contract pair.
management_rules: Close if back-month IV rises 5 vol points above entry.
NEVER allow the front long legs to expire while the back shorts remain.
exit_rules: Close the entire structure no later than 5 trading days before the FRONT (long) legs expire.
Close either short leg immediately if |delta| >= 0.85 or extrinsic <= $0.10.
Close the short call before any ex-dividend where extrinsic < dividend per share.
Buy back both shorts before selling the longs when legging out.
At level 3 the only valid action is rejection at entry.
assignment_risk: Two long-dated short legs, exposed for months, with the hedge expiring first. One of them is nearly always ITM. Dividend risk on the call, interest-carry exercise risk on the put. This is the worst assignment profile in the family.
buying_power: Naked short straddle margin on the back month: typically the greater of 20% of underlying value minus OTM amount plus premium, applied to the larger side, plus the premium of the other side.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 both expiries; back-month spread <= $0.15. Exits are risk-driven, so execution quality is critical.
common_mistakes: Mistaking it for a defined-risk trade; holding past front expiry; using it when a simple short strangle achieves the same short-vega exposure with cleaner margin and no expiry cliff.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
